llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only prompt-engineering guide that asks for no credentials, installs nothing, and its instructions are coherent with its stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (build better prompts) align with the content: four prompt frameworks, examples, troubleshooting, and production guidance. No unexpected credentials, binaries, or external services are requested.

It does not direct the agent to read files, access system state, contact external endpoints, or exfiltrate data. It does mention adversarial inputs (e.g., 'ignore all previous instructions...') as things to test, but only in an educational context.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: teach prompt frameworks and provide examples. It's instruction-only, asks for nothing sensitive, and installs nothing. Things to consider before using: 1) When copying examples into production prompts, avoid including adversarial phrasings (e.g., 'ignore all previous instructions') in contexts where system-level or policy instructions must remain enforced. 2) The guidance recommends refusal paths and output caps — implement those in your deployment to reduce abuse. 3) As with any prompt guidance, test outputs with your actual model and safety settings before using at scale.
llm.findings: [ignore-previous-instructions] expected: The phrase appears in the guidance as an example/adversarial input to test against, not as an instruction to perform malicious actions or to read external secrets. The presence of this pattern is consistent with teaching about prompt-injection risks.
